one_line: An expert laughing with the boxed book in frame one, then one comment word that delivers a discount link.

q1_hook.what: 0:00 low static shot: a woman sits cross-legged on a rug, laughing, tilting a white box. Voiceover (transcript): "למה כשאני מתרגשת יש לי פרצוף". Subtitle "למה כשאני". 0:01 the MeBook.ai logo on the box turns to the lens.
q1_hook.why: A person laughing and speaking at 0:00, with the box and its logo in hand by 1.5 s, gives warmth and a product in motion (H4, S1, H1). Subtitle and voice start together (H6). The joke is about her face, so "I wrote a book" only lands at 0:07 to 0:13 (H2).

beats.what: She laughs, holds up the MeBook.ai box; "למה כשאני", "יש לי פרצוף"
beats.why: A face, a laugh and the brand box at once

beats.what: She cuts the box open with scissors; "אבל", "כי מדובר", "הראשון"
beats.why: The unboxing builds a little suspense

beats.what: "קלינאית שאתם מכירים כתבה ספר"; she lifts the lid; "אני!", "קבלו"
beats.why: The news lands: she wrote the book

beats.what: She lifts the book out and holds the cover to the lens, laughing; the title appears as text
beats.why: The cover reveal held back until the news is out

beats.what: She flips the book in her lap; "אבל מיבוק אחראים על העיצוב", "לא של ילד גנרי"
beats.why: Says who does what and the personalising idea

beats.what: She hugs the book at 0:45; "הספר שכתבתי מכיל", "מחקרית", "לעזור"
She reads the story aloud, the book facing her; word-by-word subtitles; "וצועקת: ״מכה!״"
beats.why: A free sample of the content, in her voice

beats.what: A dim frame with sparkles, a sticker "הספר הראשון שלי", her handle; voice: "גיבי לינק בתגובות"
beats.why: The ask, spoken only, at the very end

q2_flow.interaction_prompts: Comment the word "לינק" to get a discounted link: spoken at 1:22 (transcript) and in the caption. No question, tag, save or send ask.
q2_flow.why: A funny opener, an unboxing and a held-back cover carry the first 25 s (K1, R3). The value comes at 0:27, then 0:40 to 1:21 is one static take with only subtitle changes (R1, E2). The read-aloud is a real sample but the pages face her (F5), and the CTA lands after 29 s of reading (R4).

q3_cta.what: Spoken at 1:22 to 1:24 (transcript): "לקישור עם הנחה, גיבי לינק בתגובות". Not written in the last frames. Caption: "הגיבו ״לינק״ בתגובות ואשלח לכם קישור עם הנחה כמובן". No price or code.
q3_cta.why: One action, comment a word, that delivers a concrete thing, a discount link (C1, C3, R6). It is said, and written in the caption, but not shown on screen and only at the final 2 s, after 29 s of reading (C6). The word is a plain Hebrew word.

q4_shown.what: 0:01 the MeBook.ai box front. 0:19 to 0:25 the cover with a toddler and title, held to the lens. 0:27 to 0:50 the book in hands, a hug at 0:45. 0:52 to 1:21 the open book faces her. No app, price or child.
q4_shown.why: A named professional vouches first-hand as the book's author (S6). The cover with its title is held near the lens for about 5 s (S2 partly, F4). The book is never shown being personalised, and the pages face her, not the viewer (S8, F5 not met). No child on screen matches LumeBook's own rule (S5).

q5_edit.what: About 6 shots in 84 s (first-pass count), about 14 s each, a fixed low camera with a move in close at 0:49 to 0:52. Word-by-word subtitles change every 1 to 2 s. A dimmed transition with sparkles at 1:21, then a sticker end card.
q5_edit.why: Short subtitle cards keep a long, almost uncut take readable and give a pulse (E4, T2). But 84 s of near-static footage is long for this message, the read-aloud alone is 29 s, and the end is a dimmed card (R1, R2, E8).

q6_topic.what: A speech-language pathologist announces the first book she wrote, personalised for each child, built on language-encouragement ideas for ages 0 to 3. Serves parents who want first-words help.
q6_topic.why: A first-words concern for children 0 to 3, from a professional parents already follow, gives a clear need (K6, S6). Her excited laugh is the positive peak (K1). "Research-based principles" is a spoken claim with nothing on screen to check (K4).

q7_filmed.what: A phone propped low on a rug, one medium shot: a woman sits cross-legged in a daylit room, holds the box and cover to the lens, then looks down to read. Her legs and a patterned rug fill the lower third.
q7_filmed.why: A propped phone in a real room with a person talking to the lens looks like a creator (H8, F6, F7). The cover held up fills the frame (F4). While reading she looks down, losing eye contact, and the low angle gives the lower third to legs and rug (F6).

q8_text.on_screen: White bold subtitles with a dark outline, centred at about 50% of the frame height, one to three words per card, changing every 1 to 2 s, key words larger: "למה כשאני" (0:00), "יש לי פרצוף" (0:01), "כתבה ספר" (0:13), "קבלו" (0:16), "לא של ילד גנרי" (0:37), "מחקרית" (0:42), "וצועקת: ״מכה!״" (1:01). Sticker "הספר הראשון שלי" and her handle at 1:22. No headline card, no CTA text.
q8_text.caption: "🧡💜הספר הראשון שלי💜🧡". About 115 words: the news, how it works (choose her book, enter 3 photos), what is inside, ages 0 to 3, the comment-word ask, then 4 hashtags. The tie to the brand is "כתבתי לחברת @mebook.ai".
q8_text.why: Subtitles of the speech let a muted viewer follow (T1) in short chunks, clear of the bottom 35% (T2, T4), but they sit over the book and her hands at times (T2). The caption states the product and how to buy, with 4 hashtags (T7), and the partnership is only implied by "כתבתי לחברת" (T8).

weak_points: 84 s with the product value at 0:27; a 29 s read-aloud with the pages turned from the viewer; the CTA only spoken in the last 2 s; no app or price; an unchecked research claim.
lumebook_takeaway: Film one propped phone take at floor level: the box, the cover held to the lens, then one comment-word CTA written on screen. No child needed.
not_verified: Whether the take is truly uncut (hidden jump cuts); music (cannot hear); whether the cover child comes from a real photo; the spoken name of the author (misheard in the transcript). Correction to src/coded: the read-aloud does not show the book's content to the viewer, because the open book faces her; the end card shows no CTA text in the last frames (1:21, 1:22.5), so the CTA is spoken only.
